correctness.summary: After subtracting subspace-matched intrinsic volumes, induction makes the residual vanish on every lower-dimensional cone. Stabilization by a fixed line and the same induction make it vanish on every cone containing a line. Bounded Borel regularity makes the continuous orthoscheme pullback L1, so Lotz's residual vanishing theorem applies. The one-dimensional orthogonal base case and the exact sup-norm identity are elementary and were checked separately.

limitations: Both boundedness and Borel measurability are assumed.
Unbounded measurable invariant valuations are not classified.
Boundedness alone is not shown to imply measurability.
Only real-valued scalar valuations in finite dimension are covered.
The proof uses the recent L1 orthoscheme vanishing theorem as an input.
The very recent surrounding literature leaves a residual risk of unindexed or differently phrased parallel observations.
Independent audit has not been performed.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Lotz's new conic theorem is advertised under continuity, though its final vanishing step only needs an L1 orthoscheme restriction. Knoerr's measurable result concerns Euclidean polytopes, while his spherical classification is stated under continuity; Lotz's other automatic-continuity result assumes monotonicity. Targeted literature and SCOPE searches did not locate the bounded-Borel conic classification, unique automatic extension, or the isometric l-infinity norm statement.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result weakens the regularity hypothesis in the spherical/conic Hadwiger classification from continuity to bounded Borel measurability on the polyhedral domain and proves that this weaker condition automatically restores continuity. It also gives a complete finite-dimensional norm description by subspace evaluations.
